text:
jing: Quick report — after int8 bring-up for aurora-v3 on the vertical CJK eval (mixed Han/Hanja + ruby), we see a consistent BLEU drop vs fp16. Baseline fp16 BLEU=28.4, int8 BLEU=25.1. chrF dropped 0.038.

alex: Ugh, that's sizable for a single quant step. Did you run tokenizer diffs? vertical text can sneak in fullwidth spaces/U+3000 or ZWJ changes.

jing: Yup. Ran tokenizer debug on 200 samples. Found ~0.6% extra token splits where han+ruby sequences get broken. Example:
```
FP16 tokens: [漢字, ・, ふりがな]
INT8 tokens: [漢, 字, ・, ふ, り, が, な]
```
Seems like merge tokens lost for some grapheme sequences.

marta: Did you use the same tokenizer model file for the int8 build? Sometimes packaging swaps to a fallback vocab during packaging.

jing: Confirmed same vocab blob sha256. Packaging step reuses tokenizer.bin from release artifact.

tae: Could this be an input normalization/DETOK mismatch at eval time? Are we detokenizing with the exact same detok config? vertical linewrap could insert U+200B/ZWSP.

jing: Evaluated detok config — identical. But noticed that the int8 runtime path applies an extra normalizer pass in the kernel to fold fullwidth spaces to ASCII spaces for batch padding — that might be running before tokenization in our test harness by accident.

devon: If the runtime pre-normalizer is folding U+3000 -> 0x20 before tokenization, that could change subtoken boundaries. Need to confirm order: normalize -> tokenize or tokenize -> normalize.

jing: Repro steps I used:
```bash
python infra/eval.py \
  --model aurora-v3 \
  --checkpoint /runs/aurora-v3/int8/2026-03-15 \
  --quant int8 \
  --dataset eval/cjk-vertical-hanja-2026 \
  --detok-config configs/detok/vertical.yml \
  --num-batches 200
```
Logs: sample diff printed for id=vcjh_00321:
```
REF: 漢字（注）ふりがな
PRED_FP16: 漢字（注）ふりがな
PRED_INT8: 漢 字 （ 注 ） ふ り が な
```

eval-bot: Automated bisect suggestion: run `git bisect` across quant commits between c3f1... and d4a2... or run `--quant-mode perchannel` vs `symmetric` to check kernel rounding.

alex: Also try a shadow run: serve int8 binary but swap tokenizer to fp16 runtime path (if possible) to isolate whether it's tokenization vs inference numeric error.

marta: If tokenizer is identical, another hypothesis: KV cache handling for vertical encoding changed attention masking shapes causing different prefix merges. Any attention masking logs?

jing: I pulled a small attention trace; no masking shape mismatch, but observed slightly different log-prob distributions at subtoken boundaries (spikes). Numeric noise could push beam to split.

tae: For immediate mitigation, can you try q-dequantizing only the transformer weights (keep embedding & tokenization FP16)? If embeddings remain fp16, boundary behavior might be preserved.

jing: Good idea — I'll run an ablation: quantize all vs quantize transformer-only vs quantize excluding embeddings. Planning runs now, ETA ~45m.

devon: If ablation confirms embeddings sensitive, we should add a regression test: a small suite of vertical CJK examples that must keep identical tokenization/detok across quant variants.

jing: Agreed — adding test to nightly. Will post results in this thread. Thanks for the pointers. :raised_hands:
